One organisation inside the only facet on this map with a complete public register — registration is required for essentially every interventional trial run in or submitted to the United States. WHY IT MATTERS. The register exists because a law requires it, after sponsors were found abandoning trials with unfavourable results unpublished. Every other facet here is argued about with figures the industry chose to release; this one is not.

-84.34950,33.91710.name: Atlanta Center for Reproductive Medicine
-84.34950,33.91710.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Kathryn C. Calhoun, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-122.34775,37.93576.name: California Department of Public Health - Richmond Laboratories
-122.34775,37.93576.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of California Department of Public Health. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

1.14155,52.57831.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. -89.66376,35.50427.name: Brinley Thetford
-89.66376,35.50427.desc: Carrier registered with USDA APHIS under the Animal Welfare Act, certificate 63-T-0458. Rats, mice and birds bred for research are excluded from the Act's definition of an animal — the overwhelming majority of animals used, and the great majority of the genetically altered ones. What is covered here is dogs, cats, primates, rabbits, guinea pigs, hamsters and farm animals. The rest is counted nowhere.

-64.48398,48.83343.name: Cégep de la Gaspésie et des Îles
-64.48398,48.83343.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, June 2025
-64.48398,48.83343.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, June 2025. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-43.93948,-19.92935.name: Huntington PrÃ³-Criar Medicina Reprodutiva
-43.93948,-19.92935.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: https://www.procriar.com.br/. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

-122.39600,37.66880.name: Twist Bioscience
-122.39600,37.66880.desc: Twist prints DNA to order on silicon, which made synthesis cheap enough to be routine. It is among the largest suppliers in the world and one of the firms that screens orders against lists of dangerous sequences — voluntarily, because no law requires it. That places a private company at the most consequential control point in the industry: everything downstream, in every facet of this map, begins as a sequence somebody ordered from a supplier like this one.

-84.09070,9.92810.name: Comisión Técnica Nacional de Bioseguridad
-84.09070,9.92810.desc: Costa Rica permits engineered crops to be grown for seed export while not authorising them for domestic cultivation. Seed multiplication for northern markets happens in tropical countries because two or three generations a year are possible there, so a country can host the production of a crop its own farmers may not plant.

-84.09070,9.92810.name: Federación Costarricense para la Conservación del Ambiente (FECON)
-84.09070,9.92810.desc: The Costa Rican ecological federation, which holds a seat on the national technical biosafety commission and used it to say publicly that the commission had no intention of changing its permissive practice and would remain a processing department. That is an unusual position to be able to document: a critic inside the body granting the permits, describing how it works, on the record. The federation also organised the municipal declaration campaign that produced the canton-level prohibitions, and argued that a permit issued for land inside a canton with a moratorium could be unconstitutional or at least violate municipal autonomy — the argument that reached the constitutional chamber.

1.22000,52.62200.name: Tropic Biosciences
1.22000,52.62200.desc: A UK company editing bananas and coffee, crops propagated clonally and therefore hard to improve by breeding. Clonal crops are where editing has the strongest technical case, and bananas are facing a disease that conventional breeding has not solved.

-1.51970,12.37140.name: SOFITEX — Société Burkinabè des Fibres Textiles
-1.51970,12.37140.desc: Burkina Faso began field trials in 2003 with Monsanto, which agreed to cross the Bt gene into local varieties; those went to farmers in 2008, and by 2014 the country had more engineered-crop growers than anywhere else in Africa, over 140,000 of them smallholders. Then the companies withdrew it. The Burkinabè cotton the Bt trait was crossed into came from a seventy-year breeding programme built for staple length and ginning ratio, and the engineered cultivars produced shorter lint and less of it — by 2013/14 more than two thirds of the national crop had dropped to the lower-quality medium staple class, with the ginning ratio below the 42 per cent the non-engineered cultivars reached. Cottonseed went from 53 per cent Bt in 2015/16 to a planned 30 per cent the following season and a full return to conventional seed for 2017/18, and the cotton companies asked Monsanto for compensation reported at around 280 million dollars. Note who bore the loss and who did not: farmers sold at a guaranteed price and were largely unaffected, so the failure registered only because it landed on the companies. A trait can raise yield and still destroy the value of the crop, and yield is what the trials measured.

76.63940,12.29580.name: Vipragen Biosciences
76.63940,12.29580.desc: An end-to-end preclinical contract research organisation serving pharmaceutical, biotechnology, veterinary, nutraceutical and herbal clients in India and abroad, with a vivarium holding OECD good laboratory practice, national testing accreditation and international laboratory animal care accreditation since 2013. It works to the guideline sets of the US food and drug administration, the US environmental protection agency, the World Health Organization and five pharmacopoeias, and it has agreements with a European regulatory consultancy and with Indian medical and scientific institutes. The detail worth keeping is the breadth of the standards list: a mid-sized Indian laboratory holds accreditation to more regulatory regimes than most of the regulators on this map hold jurisdictions.
